title: Transaction Coordinator
description:
# Senior Part-Time Transaction Coordinator — Real Estate Wholesaling



We are seeking an experienced, highly organized Transaction Coordinator to support our residential real estate wholesaling operations in Washington and Texas.



This is not an entry-level position. Applicants must have at least five years of hands-on transaction-coordination experience with a U.S.-based real estate wholesaling or investment company. Conventional real estate brokerage experience by itself does not satisfy this requirement.



## Schedule



* Part-time: four hours per day

* Monday through Friday

* Approximately 20 hours per week

* Must work during agreed-upon Pacific Time business hours

* Target start date: September 10, 2026

* Long-term position for the right candidate



## Primary Responsibilities



* Manage wholesale transactions from executed purchase agreement through closing

* Open title and escrow files promptly and submit complete transaction packages

* Prepare and send approved purchase agreements, assignment agreements, addenda, extensions, amendments, and related documents

* Track earnest money, inspection periods, closing dates, contingencies, signatures, and other critical deadlines

* Coordinate with sellers, cash buyers, acquisition managers, disposition managers, title companies, escrow officers, attorneys, and internal leadership

* Follow up consistently on outstanding title requirements and closing conditions

* Maintain accurate transaction stages, notes, documents, and tasks inside GoHighLevel

* Monitor buyer deposits, proof of funds, assignment documents, access arrangements, and closing confirmations

* Identify and immediately escalate issues involving probate, trusts, powers of attorney, deceased owners, liens, judgments, occupancy, missing signatures, or title defects

* Provide professional and timely updates to sellers and buyers

* Maintain an organized transaction checklist and electronic file for every property

* Deliver a daily written report showing completed tasks, approaching deadlines, and unresolved blockers

* Support the company’s existing Transaction Coordinator and Sales Operations Manager



## Required Qualifications



* At least five years of hands-on transaction-coordination experience with U.S. real estate wholesalers or investors

* Demonstrated experience with assignment transactions, cash purchases, double closings, title companies, and escrow

* Experience managing multiple active transactions simultaneously

* Strong understanding of purchase agreements, assignment agreements, addenda, earnest money, title commitments, settlement statements, and closing timelines

* Excellent written and spoken English

* Strong follow-up, documentation, and deadline-management skills

* Ability to recognize transaction risks and escalate problems before they delay a closing

* Professional experience communicating directly with sellers, buyers, title companies, and attorneys

* High attention to detail and ability to work independently

* Reliable high-speed internet, quiet workspace, and backup internet or power

* Willingness to complete a paid skills assessment and provide professional references



## Preferred Experience



* GoHighLevel

* Google Workspace

* DocuSign or similar electronic-signature platforms

* PropStream

* Washington or Texas real estate transactions

* Probate, inherited-property, trust, and power-of-attorney transactions

* Occupied properties and cash-for-keys coordination

* Creating transaction checklists and standard operating procedures



## Performance Expectations



* All new files opened with title or escrow on the same business day

* No missed contractual deadlines

* All outstanding signatures and documents actively tracked

* Material title or legal issues escalated within one business day

* Every transaction record kept complete and current

* Professional and timely communication with internal and external parties

* Daily visibility into every transaction’s status, next action, responsible party, and blocker



## How to Apply



Begin your application by answering the following questions:



1. How many years have you worked specifically as a Transaction Coordinator for U.S. real estate wholesalers or investors?

2. Approximately how many wholesale transactions have you helped close?

3. What was the largest number of active transactions you managed simultaneously?

4. Explain your experience with assignment agreements, double closings, earnest money, and title companies.

5. Describe a difficult title, probate, trust, lien, or power-of-attorney issue you identified and helped escalate or resolve.

6. Which transaction-management and CRM platforms have you used?

7. What four-hour working schedule can you maintain in Pacific Time?

8. What is your requested hourly or monthly compensation?

9. Do you have reliable backup internet and power?

10. Please provide a résumé and a short voice or video introduction.



Applications that do not demonstrate at least five years of real estate wholesaling transaction-coordination experience will not be considered.

title: Project Manager
description:
We are seeking a detail-oriented Technical Project Manager to coordinate construction-related orders and ensure that the products being approved, ordered, manufactured, and shipped match the requirements of each project.



The primary responsibility of this position is technical and organizational accuracy. You will compare project requirements against supplier-submitted line drawings, specifications, order confirmations, and shipping records. You will identify discrepancies, obtain missing information, and make sure requirements are satisfied before items move into production or shipment.



This is not a general administrative project-management position. Candidates must have practical experience reading and interpreting architectural, construction, shop, or fabrication drawings.



Supplier pricing and commercial negotiations are handled by another team member. This role is responsible for technical compliance, documentation, coordination, and project tracking.



## Key Responsibilities



- Review project drawings, schedules, specifications, purchase requirements, and related documents to understand exactly what is required.

- Review and approve supplier-submitted line drawings and shop drawings against approved project requirements and specifications.

- Compare supplier drawings, product data, order confirmations, and other submittals to the applicable project documents.

- Verify dimensions, quantities, configurations, finishes, materials, hardware, accessories, tolerances, and other specified requirements.

- Confirm that what is ordered matches what was approved and required for the project.

- Identify drawing discrepancies, omissions, scope gaps, dimensional conflicts, and specification deviations before production begins.

- Clearly mark up drawings and prepare organized comments for supplier revisions.

- Maintain approval records and ensure that suppliers and internal teams are working from the latest document revisions.

- Coordinate technical questions and missing information with suppliers, internal team members, designers, contractors, and North American stakeholders.

- Escalate substitutions, exceptions, and unresolved technical issues for management approval when they fall outside established requirements or approval authority.

- Track items from initial request through drawing approval, order placement, production, shipment, delivery, and closeout.

- Maintain accurate order trackers showing quantities, approval status, production status, expected completion dates, shipping dates, tracking details, delivery status, and outstanding issues.

- Monitor production and shipping milestones and follow up when information or documentation is overdue.

- Confirm that shipping documents and item quantities correspond with the approved order.

- Provide concise project updates identifying current status, upcoming deadlines, discrepancies, risks, and decisions required.

- Maintain organized project folders containing specifications, drawings, revisions, approvals, purchase records, and shipping documents.

- Help improve checklists, trackers, templates, and standard procedures for drawing review and order management.



## Required Qualifications



- At least three years of relevant experience in construction coordination, architectural coordination, project management, drafting, engineering, procurement coordination, estimating, manufacturing, or a related field.

- Demonstrated ability to read and interpret architectural drawings, construction drawings, line drawings, shop drawings, or fabrication drawings.

- Strong understanding of dimensions, drawing scales, elevations, sections, details, schedules, specifications, annotations, and revision markings.

- Experience comparing supplier submittals or product information against drawings and written specifications.

- Strong attention to detail and the ability to identify inconsistencies across multiple documents.

- Experience maintaining order, procurement, production, or shipping trackers.

- Excellent written and spoken English.

- Clear and professional written communication when requesting corrections or explaining technical discrepancies.

- Ability to manage multiple projects and document revisions without losing track of details.

- Ability to work independently, prioritize assignments, and follow issues through to resolution.

- Reliable computer, high-speed internet connection, and a suitable remote-working environment.

- Availability for scheduled overlap with both Asian and North American business hours.



## Preferred Qualifications



- Education or professional experience in architecture, civil engineering, construction management, interior design, drafting, manufacturing, or a related discipline.

- Experience supporting construction projects in the United States or Canada.

- Experience reviewing millwork, cabinetry, doors, windows, fixtures, finishes, architectural products, or other manufactured construction components.

- Familiarity with both imperial and metric measurements and the ability to convert between them accurately.

- Experience reviewing product data sheets, finish schedules, hardware schedules, material submittals, or samples.

- Familiarity with AutoCAD, Bluebeam, Adobe Acrobat, Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud, 
, Asana, ClickUp, Smartsheet, or similar tools.

- Understanding of manufacturing lead times, international shipping milestones, and basic quality-control procedures.



The ability to prepare original CAD drawings is helpful but not required. The essential requirement is the ability to accurately interpret, compare, mark up, and approve supplier drawings against established project requirements.



## Scope of Authority



The Technical Project Manager may approve supplier drawings when they fully comply with documented project requirements and established approval procedures.



Any substitution, material change, dimensional deviation, specification exception, or unresolved conflict must be documented and escalated to the appropriate internal decision-maker. The contractor is not expected to provide licensed architectural or engineering services or approve changes requiring a licensed professional.



## Working Schedule



This role follows a hybrid remote schedule designed to support suppliers in Asia and projects in North America.



The regular schedule will include:



- Daytime availability in the Philippines for supplier coordination.

- Scheduled evening overlap with the North American team.

- Approximately 40 working hours per week.

- A mutually agreed schedule with appropriate breaks between working periods.

- Occasional schedule adjustments for important meetings, production deadlines, or urgent project issues.



The exact working hours and required North American time-zone overlap will be confirmed during the interview.



## Contractor Arrangement



This is an independent-contractor engagement rather than an employee position.



The contractor will:



- Be responsible for their own taxes, government contributions, insurance, equipment, internet service, and home-office expenses.

- Provide services remotely using their own suitable workspace and equipment.

- Invoice the company according to the agreed payment schedule.

- Receive the agreed contractor fee without employee benefits unless a particular benefit is expressly included in the written contractor agreement.

- Be evaluated based on deliverables, accuracy, responsiveness, and compliance with agreed project procedures.



The final agreement will define the scope of services, payment terms, schedule expectations, confidentiality obligations, and termination provisions.



## What Success Looks Like



Within the first 90 days, the successful contractor should be able to:



- Understand our products, project requirements, and document-control procedures.

- Independently compare supplier line drawings against project drawings and specifications.

- Identify missing, conflicting, or noncompliant information before an order enters production.

- Produce clear drawing markups and correction requests.

- Maintain accurate records of approvals, revisions, orders, production status, and shipments.

- Provide reliable status reports without requiring frequent reminders.

- Prevent costly mistakes by ensuring that approved, ordered, produced, and shipped items match project requirements.



## How to Apply



Please provide:



1. A short introduction describing your relevant experience.

2. Your résumé.

3. Examples of construction, architectural, manufacturing, or procurement projects you have coordinated.

4. A description of the drawings and specifications you have reviewed.

5. Examples of products or construction components you have tracked from approval through delivery.

6. The software and project-tracking systems you have used.

7. Your desired monthly contractor fee in U.S. dollars.

8. Your availability for hybrid Philippine and North American working hours.



Begin your application with the words **“Technical Drawing Review”** so we know you carefully reviewed the posting.



Shortlisted candidates will be asked to complete a brief paid practical exercise. The exercise may include comparing a supplier line drawing against project requirements, identifying discrepancies, preparing drawing comments, and updating a sample order tracker.

title: Experienced Operations Manager
description:
OPERATIONS MANAGER (PATH TO DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS)



Independent contractor, full time hours.

Remote. You must be able to work US Eastern Time hours.

$1,400 to $1,800 USD per month depending on experience, plus performance bonuses.

Reports directly to the CEO.



WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

Our Operations Manager is moving into a COO seat. Before that can happen, someone has to take the department off their hands.

That is the job. Not filling a vacancy. You are inheriting a functioning department from the person who built it, while they are still here to hand it over properly.

You will be trained directly by them, then given real ownership of what they were carrying.



BEFORE YOU KEEP READING

We get a lot of applications for roles like this and most are rejected in under a minute. Not because the people are bad, but because they did not read the posting or they do not have the experience it asks for.

So, plainly: if you have not run operations for a real business before, this is not your role. Stop here. It will save us both the time.



If you have, keep going. We are genuinely looking for you and there are not many of you.



THE BUSINESS

A $7M+ education and mentorship company. 140+ active students, plus partnerships, offer launches, webinars and multi day challenge events.

It moves fast and the standard is high. We over deliver and we expect the same from the person running operations.



WHAT YOU WILL OWN

Daily operations across offer launches, webinars and multi day events

Launch and project management: timelines, deliverables and cross team coordination, so every launch ships on time and nothing slips



Building, documenting, maintaining and ENFORCING SOPs, so the business runs on systems rather than on any one person

Meeting coordination and team accountability: keeping people on their tasks, deliverables and daily reporting

Taking work off the current Operations Manager so they can step into their COO role. This is your primary mandate and how you will be judged.



Making sure the executive level work the CEO and leadership set lands on time and to standard

A direct line to the CEO. You surface problems fast. No filters, no surprises.



WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU

You have actually held an operations manager or ops lead role, running operations for a real business. An executive assistant trying the role for the first time is not a fit.

A track record you can walk us through: businesses you have operated, launches you have run, teams you have managed

Clear, professional English, spoken and written. You will be understood easily on calls with the team, clients and stakeholders.



Genuinely comfortable on the phone and on camera. You will be on calls every day.

Systems minded. You build and enforce process, not just follow it.

A self starter who owns outcomes. You are not looking to be handed tasks all day.

Obsessively detail oriented. You triple check your work.

Your own reliable computer, a stable connection good enough for daily video calls, and a quiet space to take them from



MANDATORY SKILLS

Operations management. You have held the role before, at a real business.

SOP development, documentation and enforcement

Project management and launch management

Team management and accountability

English, spoken and written, at a professional level

Confident on video calls and phone calls, daily

Time management and prioritization

Attention to detail



STRONGLY PREFERRED

Experience in coaching, education or info product businesses

Webinar and multi day challenge event operations

Managing remote or distributed teams

Hiring and onboarding

Project management tools such as ClickUp, Asana, Notion or Monday

CRM and automation platforms

You do not need to have used our exact tools. You do need to pick up new systems fast.



WHO THIS IS NOT FOR

Executive assistants presenting themselves as operations managers

People who need to be told what to do all day

Anyone without real, prior operations management experience



Anyone juggling three or four other clients where things fall through the cracks. This is not a side gig.

We build long term. Our current Operations Manager has worked with the owner 3.5+ years. Team members have been here 2+ years. We are looking for someone who wants to grow as the company scales, not someone passing through.



SCHEDULE

These are our operating windows. Final hours are agreed with you before the engagement begins.



Monday to Friday: 1:00 PM to 10:00 PM ET. A 9 hour window with a 1 hour break, roughly 8 hours worked.

Saturday: until 12:00 PM ET, half day

Sunday: a short 2 hour window before 12:00 PM ET, to prep the week ahead



Approximately 46 hours per week. We are telling you this up front rather than after you are invested. It is a demanding schedule and it includes weekend hours. If that does not work for your life, this is the moment to say so, and there is no hard feeling in it. As an independent contractor you control how you deliver the work. These windows reflect when the business runs and when the team needs you reachable.



COMPENSATION

Base $1,400 to $1,800 USD per month depending on experience

Performance bonuses after a 60 to 90 day ramp. Criteria and targets are agreed with you in writing before the ramp ends, based on the measures below. Paid monthly. You are responsible for your own taxes and any registrations required where you are based.



HOW YOU WILL BE MEASURED

Work successfully taken off the current Operations Manager. This is the primary measure.

Full ownership of your department

SOP compliance and on time launch delivery

Team accountability: meetings run, people on their deliverables

Executive level work delivered on schedule Specific targets are agreed in writing during your first 30 days. You will always know what you are being measured against.



YOUR FIRST FEW MONTHS

Weeks 1 and 2: shadow the current Operations Manager. Step in wherever you can take responsibility. Learn the business and the process.



Ramp: take ownership of a department. Report directly to the CEO. Become the operator the business runs with.

Then: demonstrated ownership opens the path to Director of Operations.



Advancement is based on performance and business need. It is the path we are hiring for and we mean it, but it is not a guaranteed timeline and we are not going to pretend otherwise to get you in the door.

The first 90 days are a mutual trial. Either side may end the engagement in that period with written notice.



CONFIDENTIALITY

This role touches client information, financials and internal systems. A confidentiality agreement is signed before you start. Client names, numbers and internal conversations do not leave the business.



WHAT WE DELETE WITHOUT READING:

Copy pasted applications that could have gone to any job



Anything written entirely by AI with no specifics in it

Anyone who has not read far enough to know the schedule

Shortlisted candidates go through a scenario based interview. We will hand you real operational problems and ask how you would fix them. It is not a checklist of tools.



Come ready to show how you think and what you have actually done.

We verify what you tell us. References and confirmation of the experience described may be requested before an offer. If it is embellished, it surfaces at the reference stage and we will not move forward.



Every application is considered on the strength of the experience presented.



HOW TO APPLY

title: Dispatch Operations Specialist

You’ll be working across multiple systems and communication channels, keeping track of what’s happening across different markets and jumping in when something needs attention. You’ll work closely with field operators and internal teams, make quick calls when issues come up, and speak directly with customers when needed. 



This is a hands-on role for someone who is comfortable making quick decisions, switching between different tools, and working with both internal teams and external customers. You’ll be working closely with U.S.-based field teams every shift, so previous experience supporting U.S. operations remotely is a strong plus. Since this function is still being built, you’ll also have a real opportunity to help shape the workflows, escalation paths, and processes that the team will use as it grows.



What You'll Do

- Monitor fleet activity and alert channels across multiple platforms and markets, tracking robot and vehicle locations, battery levels, active tasks, and delivery status.

- Own operational issues through resolution by identifying and prioritizing issues as they arise, including stalled or  immobilized robots, unsafe conditions, missed tasks, and deliveries that fall off schedule.

- Contact the assigned field operator to resolve the issue, and follow established escalation procedures when they do not respond within the required timeframe.

- Coordinate backup coverage when the assigned operator is unavailable so that fleet operations continue without interruption.

- Continuously triage incoming alerts, messages, and fleet data, determining what requires immediate action and what can be handled through normal workflows.

- Prioritize and coordinate field service activity across markets, including battery swaps, robot recoveries, fleet interventions, and other service stops.

- Handle calls from drivers and supervisors on active runs who are unable to locate a delivery address or reach a customer, and resolve the issue on their behalf.

- Contact customers directly to confirm delivery locations, obtain access instructions, or complete a drop off.

- Document each i
, the actions taken, and any details relevant to future operations - such as gate codes, difficult access points, and recurring problem locations - and help pinpoint recurring patterns that can improve future workflows and customer technology.

- Contribute to the development of dispatch procedures, escalation paths, and operational documentation as the operation grows.

- Work across multiple customer platforms, dashboards, Slack channels, and internal tools, quickly building context even when information is spread across different systems.



What We're Looking For

- 3+ years of experience in dispatch, logistics, fleet operations, transportation, field operations, or another fast-moving operations environment.

- At least 1 year of experience working directly with a startup is highly preferred

- Experience supporting U.S.-based companies, customers, drivers, operators, or field teams, preferably in a remote or offshore setup.

- Hands-on experience coordinating drivers, field workers, technicians, couriers, vehicles, deliveries, or other moving resources.

- Strong real-time problem-solving skills. You can assess a situation quickly, figure out what needs to happen, and take action without waiting to be told every step.

- Comfortable handling multiple tasks, systems, and communication channels at the same time, as well as piecing together information across multiple tools when troubleshooting an issue.

- Confident in communicating with customers, drivers, operators, and internal teams, including people you may be interacting with for the first time.

- Comfortable making outbound calls and speaking with unfamiliar customers, drivers, and operators in real time.

- Strong, natural English communication skills, both written and verbal.

- Strong documentation skills with the ability to clearly capture what happened, what was done, and what needs to happen next.

- Comfortable working with technology and learning unfamiliar platforms quickly.

- Able to stay calm, organized, and responsive when several time-sensitive issues happen at once.

- Comfortable working in a startup environment where processes and tools are still evolving.

- Available to work U.S.-aligned hours, including weekends or other coverage periods when needed.

- Reliable internet connection and a dependable work-from-home setup.

- Base salary: 55,000 PHP per month

- Paid Time Off and Paid Holidays

- Match every visual to the line it sits under. Most editors grab B-roll that's vaguely on-topic and the ad dies

- Iterate fast off performance data. We go through what won, what died, and why, every week

- Push the format forward. New AI tools drop every month and I want you testing them before anyone else



Why this seat is different

You'll see your numbers every day. You get a tracking sheet that refreshes daily with the performance of every ad you made: spend, hook rate, hold rate, ROAS. You always know where you stand and exactly what your bonus is doing. No guessing, no waiting for a monthly report.



Uncapped commission on ad spend. Your bonus is a percentage of the spend your winning ads carry. KPI agreed up front. A winner keeps paying you for as long as it keeps spending. No ceiling on it.



The avatar is done. We know who she is, what she believes, and what stops her scroll. You don't have to guess who you're talking to, you have to make ads that hit her. Fast.



We invest in you. You get the ecomtalent course paid for, every AI tool you need on our accounts, and if you find a new tool that makes you faster or better, tell me and we'll get it. We're always open to suggestions.



Direct access. No manager, no ticket queue. Me, the data, and you.



Where this goes

Editor → Junior Creative Strategist → Creative Strategist → Senior Creative Strategist.



Every step is a pay rise, based on performance, not time. If you start thinking about why an ad works, not just how to cut it, and you start writing your own scripts, you'll get there fast. It's earned, not automatic, and how fast you get there is on you.



You'll thrive here if

- You already live in AI video tools and get excited when a new model drops

- You think in hooks, pacing and retention, not filters and transitions

- You take blunt feedback and come back with a better cut the same day

- You're hungry. You screenshot ads you scroll past and have real opinions on why a hook works

- You want ownership, not a task list. You want to grow with the brand, not pass through it



Don't apply if

- You edit for looks, not conversions

- You've never run direct-response creative that spent real money

- You're anti-AI or "AI is a tool I use sometimes"

- You're a freelancer looking to stack another client

- You need everything spelled out before you can produce

- You go quiet when a deadline slips

None of those people last here.



The offer

- $2,000–$4,000/month base depending on where you're at

- Uncapped commission as a % of ad spend on every ad that hits our KPI, tracked daily in your sheet

- ecomtalent course, all AI tools and subscriptions paid

- Base reviewed and moved up as you produce winners and step into strategy



How to apply

Fill out the form below. It takes about 10 minutes.



👉 



Send your portfolio, your best AI-generated ad work, and a short note on which AI tools you actually use and why. Tell me about an ad you made that won and why you think it won. Don't send me a copy-paste application. Tell me why YOU want this seat specifically.



The process: form → call with me → paid trial (2 scripts, 3 hooks each) → hire. I read every application and reply either way.

title: Operations Manager — Ecommerce & Property (Hands-On Role)
description:
About us

Read this part carefully



This is a working role, not a pure management role.



About half your week is overseeing a small team. The other half is doing real work yourself — the kind that takes judgment and can't be handed to a rep: chargebacks, freight paperwork, carrier claims, marketplace issues, escalations.

Amazon Seller Central

Property management, self-storage, or leasing experience

Experience writing procedures or building workflows from scratch

Experience interviewing or onboarding remote staff



Not a fit if



You want a role where you only delegate and report

You consider hands-on work below your level

You need someone above you to make routine calls

You've only managed by being liked

What we offer

Competitive rate based on experience

Real ownership. You'll shape how this operation runs, not just execute someone else's plan

A small, established, profitable company with 25+ years of history

Direct access to the owners. No layers, no politics

Written procedures for most of what we do — and where they don't exist, you'll write them

Long-term, stable position

title: TEAM COORDINATOR / MULTILINGUAL INTERPRETER Full-Time  |  Remote — Open Worldwide  |  Reports to: Operations Manager
description:
About the Role

We're hiring a Team Coordinator / Multilingual Interpreter to support day-to-day operations for a growing language services company serving clients across the U.S. with a distributed, global team. This dual-function role blends hands-on coordination of interpreter assignments with active interpreting work of your own. You'll keep schedules, communication, and quality on track for a roster of interpreters, while also stepping in to interpret sessions in your own language pair(s). It's a great fit for someone who is both a strong organizer and a skilled linguist.

What You'll Do

Team Coordination

• Coordinate daily assignment scheduling, confirming interpreter availability well ahead of session start times.

• Serve as the point of contact for interpreters on your team — answering questions, resolving scheduling conflicts, and escalating issues as needed.

• Track and follow up on interpreter confirmations, cancellations, and no-shows, filling gaps quickly to avoid missed sessions.

• Monitor interpreter session quality using standardized quality-monitoring reports and provide constructive feedback.

• Maintain accurate records of interpreter availability, certifications, and assignment history.

• Support onboarding of new interpreters joining your team, including orientation on tools, protocols, and expectations.

• Participate in regular team check-ins to flag staffing gaps, share updates, and align on priorities.

Interpreting

• Provide accurate, professional interpretation (consecutive and/or simultaneous) in your language pair(s), following industry code of ethics and confidentiality standards.

• Interpret across settings that may include legal, medical, educational, or general business contexts, depending on assignment.

• Prepare for assignments by reviewing relevant terminology and context in advance when provided.

• Maintain professionalism, neutrality, and accuracy in every session, and document any issues encountered.

Who You Are

• Bachelor's degree required (any field).

• Proven experience as a professional interpreter, plus prior experience in scheduling, coordination, or team support.

• Fluent in English and at least one additional language, at a professional interpreting standard, across speaking, reading, and listening.

• Before applying, please test your English level using the free EF SET English Test and include your score/certificate with your application.

• Resume demonstrating proven, relevant experience, plus professional references who can confirm your work.

• Reliable home office setup: a computer, one to two additional monitors, a quiet working environment, and a stable, dependable internet connection.

• Trustworthy and self-directed — able to work independently and reliably with minimal supervision, as well as collaboratively when needed.

• Energetic and engaged, bringing genuine knowledge and judgment to the business rather than just following instructions.

• Disciplined about applying SOPs and documented processes consistently, without cutting corners.

• Strong organizational skills and comfort managing a high volume of scheduling changes under time pressure.

• Clear, professional written and verbal communication.

Nice to Have

• Court/legal or medical interpreter certification.

• Experience with interpreting/dispatch platforms or scheduling software.

• Proficiency in a third language.

• Experience supporting school district, judicial, or healthcare client accounts.

Key Performance Indicators

KPI Target Frequency

Assignment fill rate for your team (confirmed coverage before session start) ≥ 98% Weekly

On-time interpreter confirmations ≥ 95% Weekly

No-show / late cancellation rate on your team < 2% Monthly

Average client quality score for your interpreting sessions ≥ 4.5 / 5 Monthly

Team roster documentation accuracy (availability, certifications) 100% Monthly

Staffing gaps resolved within same business day ≥ 95% Weekly

SOP adherence across coordination and interpreting work 100% Ongoing

Key Skills

Interpreting

• Interpreting proficiency — accurate, professional consecutive/simultaneous interpretation in your language pair(s), following confidentiality and ethics standards.

• Clear bilingual communication (C2 English + target language) — fluent across speaking, reading, and listening.

Coordination

• Scheduling & team coordination — managing interpreter availability, confirmations, and last-minute staffing gaps under time pressure.

• Multitasking & prioritization — juggling multiple interpreters' schedules and shifting assignment needs simultaneously without dropping coverage.

• Conflict resolution — smoothing over scheduling clashes, last-minute cancellations, or interpreter/client friction calmly and quickly.

• Attention to detail & recordkeeping — keeping availability, certification, and assignment records accurate and current.

• Proactive problem-solving — spotting a coverage gap before it becomes a missed session and filling it fast.

• Time management — meeting confirmation deadlines (e.g., the 72-hour window) consistently across a full roster.

• Interpersonal/people management — coaching interpreters on quality feedback and keeping team morale steady.

• Adaptability — handling last-minute changes in client needs, session types, or language demand without losing organization.

• Basic tech fluency — comfortable learning and working across scheduling/dispatch platforms and shared trackers.

You own our pipeline. Every lead in our CRM is yours to work — fresh inbound, live conversations, deals that stalled, no-shows that need rebooking, and older leads that went quiet. On top of that, there's a much bigger market that's never heard of us at all.



Your job is simple to describe and hard to do: get them onto our closer's calendar.



You will not be running the sales calls — not at first. You book them. Our closer runs them. We're saying that plainly on purpose, because the ladder out of it is printed below with real numbers.





What you'll do every day

•⁠  ⁠Work every stage of our GoHighLevel pipeline — call, text, and
 new inbound leads, active opportunities, stalled deals, no-shows, and leads that went quiet (mostly clinics and private practices)

•⁠  ⁠Make sure nothing stalls. If a lead has been sitting untouched, that's on you.

•⁠  ⁠Prospect net-new. Cold calls, cold
, and DMs to businesses that have never heard of us. This isn't filler for slow days — it's the second door to the same number, and you'll spend real hours here.

•⁠  ⁠Book qualified discovery calls onto our closer's calendar

•⁠  ⁠Use our qualification checklist so the calls you book are real, not filler

•⁠  ⁠Follow up on a fixed cadence — nothing sits untouched

•⁠  ⁠Keep the CRM spotless: every lead has a stage, a note, and a next action with a date

•⁠  ⁠Write a short brief on every prospect before their call so the closer walks in prepared

•⁠  ⁠Sit in on discovery calls and take notes — this is how you learn the sale



One number defines your week: qualified discovery calls held. Not dials. Not conversations. Calls that happened and were worth having. Warm database or ice-cold prospect — we don't care where the call came from, only that it happened and it was real.



Where this goes. This is a starting seat, not a ceiling. Reps who consistently hit their call numbers and demonstrate they can run a conversation move up into running their own sales calls, at senior pay. We'll walk you through exactly what that path looks like on the interview.



Who this is for

•⁠  ⁠You've done real outbound — cold calls, cold DMs, cold
 — and you don't dread the phone

•⁠  ⁠Your spoken English is clear and easy for a 62-year-old clinic owner in Ohio to follow on the first pass, over a phone line

•⁠  ⁠You're organized. Nothing falls out of your CRM.

•⁠  ⁠You want to become a closer and you're willing to earn it in the trenches first

•⁠  ⁠You can be measured on one public number every week without falling apart



Who this is not for

•⁠  ⁠Anyone who wants warm leads handed to them

•⁠  ⁠Anyone who wants to run sales calls on day one — that's not this seat



Big advantages (not required)

•⁠  ⁠You've worked at a virtual assistant, staffing, outsourcing, or recruitment company in any role — including as a VA. If you've supported a US business remotely and you want to move into sales, we especially want to talk to you. You already understand our product better than most salespeople ever will.

•⁠  ⁠Healthcare or medical background — clinics are our specialty and this is our single biggest advantage to have

•⁠  ⁠You've sold to US small business owners in any industry

•⁠  ⁠GoHighLevel experience



Compensation

•⁠  ⁠$6–$8/hour, based on experience — 40 hrs/week

•⁠  ⁠$10 for every call you book that is held and passes our qualification checklist (no-shows don't count; unqualified prospects don't count)

Requirements

•⁠  ⁠Based in Latin America

•⁠  ⁠Schedule: 10:00am – 8:00pm US Eastern, Monday–Friday, with a 2-hour midday break. That's 8 working hours a day, 40 per week. You need to be genuinely available across that window — this shift exists so we can reach owners on both US coasts.

•⁠  ⁠Reliable high-speed internet, quiet workspace, working headset





How to apply

: 
 

Subject: Junior Pipeline Rep 



Send three things. Missing any one of them and we don't review the application.

1.⁠ ⁠Your CV

2.⁠ ⁠Three short written answers

A few sentences each. Specifics beat polish.



•⁠  ⁠What outbound work have you done? Roughly how many calls, DMs, or
s per day — and what were you trying to get people to do?

) or similar. 90 seconds max. One take — no script, no editing.

Building Code & Engineering Coordination

- Provide clear communication and timely revisions when adjustments are required.

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE TABLE

Structural Design Expertise

- Proven experience producing structural plans for US residential projects, such as ADUs, single-family homes, additions, or similar projects.

- Strong understanding of foundations, wood framing systems, structural connections, and load paths.

- Good to have experience in creating structural plans using helical piers.

- Ability to read, interpret, and coordinate architectural and structural Construction Drawings.

Construction & Technical Knowledge

- Hands-on understanding of how structural designs translate to real-world construction.

- Strong attention to detail and ability to identify inconsistencies between architectural and structural plans.

Code Knowledge

- Working knowledge and minimum of 2-year experience of U.S. residential building codes.

- Familiarity with IRC/IBC structural requirements.

- Experience with Connecticut building codes, residential construction, or local permitting requirements is a strong plus.



Collaboration, Communication & Accountability

- Ability to work effectively with architects, engineers, permitting teams, and construction professionals.

- Clear written and verbal English communication skills.

- Open, receptive, and responsive to feedback, with the ability to incorporate revisions efficiently.

- Strong sense of ownership and accountability for deliverables, timelines, coordination, and design accuracy.



WHAT WE OFFER

Competitive Compensation

Professional Growth

Collaborative & Supportive Culture

title: Senior Accountant / Controller
description:
Remote | Philippines | Full-Time | U.S. Accounting Experience Required



About the Role

We are a growing, family-owned U.S. firm with approximately 10 LLCs and multiple business entities. We are seeking an experienced Senior Accountant / Controller to take ownership of the day-to-day accounting and financial operations across our companies.



This is a hands-on, high-responsibility position and the successful candidate will be the sole internal accounting professional for the firm. You will work closely with company ownership, our financial advisor, and our tax team to ensure our books are accurate, current, organized, and properly maintained.



This is not a basic bookkeeping position. We are looking for an experienced accounting professional who understands U.S. accounting practices, can independently manage multiple sets of books, and is comfortable taking ownership of the full accounting cycle.



The ideal candidate is highly detail-oriented, exceptionally organized, proactive, trustworthy, and capable of managing multiple priorities and deadlines with minimal supervision.



Key Responsibilities



Multi-Entity Accounting & Bookkeeping

Serve as the primary accounting professional for approximately 10 U.S. LLCs and business entities.

Independently maintain multiple sets of books and ensure each entity's financial records are accurate, complete, and current.

Perform weekly bookkeeping and maintain all accounting activity in QuickBooks Online (QBO).

Maintain and manage the general ledger for each entity.

Perform bank, credit card, and other account reconciliations.

Properly categorize and record financial transactions across multiple entities.

Identify discrepancies, unusual transactions, and errors and take appropriate action to resolve them.

Ensure intercompany transactions and transfers are properly recorded when applicable.

Maintain organized supporting documentation for accounting transactions.

Keep books clean and current throughout the year to support financial reporting and tax preparation.



Accounts Payable & Vendor Payments

Manage the complete accounts payable process.

Review, code, and process vendor and contractor invoices.

Schedule and make payments to vendors, contractors, and other service providers.

Maintain accurate vendor records and payment documentation.

Monitor outstanding payables and ensure payments are made accurately and on time.

Communicate professionally with vendors and contractors regarding invoices, payments, and account questions.



Accounts Receivable, Invoicing & Billing

Manage the complete accounts receivable and billing process.

Prepare and issue client invoices accurately and on schedule.

Track outstanding receivables and follow up on past-due balances.

Apply payments and maintain accurate customer records.

Investigate and resolve billing discrepancies.

Communicate professionally with clients regarding billing and payment questions.

Maintain accurate billing records across multiple entities.



Payroll

Manage weekly payroll accurately and on time.

Review payroll information and supporting documentation prior to processing.

Ensure payroll-related accounting entries are properly recorded.

Maintain accurate payroll records.

Coordinate with payroll providers and management as needed.

Identify and communicate payroll discrepancies or issues promptly.



Monthly Financial Reporting

Prepare accurate monthly Profit & Loss (P&L) statements and financial reports for each entity.

Complete monthly account reconciliations and ensure books are properly maintained for month-end reporting.

Review financial statements for unusual variances, errors, or inconsistencies.

Provide management with timely and accurate financial information.

Assist with cash-flow tracking, budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis as needed.

Prepare supporting schedules and reports for management, our financial advisor, and tax team.



Tax & External Accounting Support

Work closely with the firm's financial advisor and tax team.

Provide accurate financial records, reports, reconciliations, and supporting documentation as requested.

Assist with year-end close and tax preparation.

Respond to accounting-related questions from external advisors and tax professionals.

Ensure books and records are maintained in a condition that supports an efficient year-end tax process.



Accounting Processes & Controls

Maintain organized and efficient accounting procedures across the company's entities.

Identify opportunities to improve accounting processes, reporting, and internal controls.

Maintain appropriate documentation and approval processes for financial transactions.

Proactively identify potential accounting issues and bring them to management's attention.

Help ensure financial transactions are properly documented, reviewed, and recorded.



Required Qualifications



Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field — required.

Minimum 3–5 years of progressive accounting experience — required.

Hands-on experience working with U.S.-based companies and U.S. accounting practices — required.

Demonstrated experience managing multiple companies, LLCs, or sets of books simultaneously — required.

Experience independently managing full-cycle accounting responsibilities.

Experience working with multi-entity accounting is strongly preferred.



Accounting Knowledge

Strong working knowledge of:

U.S. GAAP

General Ledger

Accounts Payable (AP)

Accounts Receivable (AR)

Payroll

Bank and credit card reconciliations

Month-end close

Financial statement preparation

Profit & Loss reporting

Cash-flow management

Multi-entity accounting

Intercompany transactions



Software & Technology

Strong hands-on experience with QuickBooks Online (QBO) — required.

Advanced/proficient Microsoft Excel skills — required.

Advanced/proficient Google Sheets skills — required.

Comfortable working with large amounts of financial data and complex spreadsheets.

Strong understanding of formulas, lookups, PivotTables, filtering, sorting, and other spreadsheet functions used for accounting and financial analysis.

Comfortable learning and working with new software and cloud-based systems.



Personal & Professional Qualifications



We are looking for someone who demonstrates:



Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.

Exceptional organization and time-management skills.

Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.

Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.

Ability to exercise sound professional judgment.

Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.

Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines simultaneously.

Strong follow-through and personal accountability.

A proactive approach to identifying and solving problems.

Ability to recognize when something does not look right and investigate it.

High level of integrity, discretion, and professionalism.

Ability to handle sensitive financial and employee information confidentially.

Ability to communicate financial issues clearly to non-accounting professionals.



What We're Looking For

We are looking for someone who will take ownership of the accounting function rather than simply complete assigned bookkeeping tasks.



The right person will be someone who:



Takes pride in maintaining clean, accurate, and organized books.

Can confidently manage multiple entities and competing priorities.

Does not need to be constantly reminded about deadlines.

Notices discrepancies and investigates them rather than simply recording them.

Thinks proactively about upcoming accounting needs.

Communicates problems early and clearly.

Is comfortable working independently and making appropriate accounting judgments.

Can build structure and organization around a multi-entity accounting environment.

Understands the importance of accuracy when dealing with payroll, vendor payments, client billing, and financial reporting.

Is trustworthy and understands the importance of protecting confidential information.



Work Schedule

This is a full-time remote position supporting U.S.-based businesses.



Monday–Friday, 6:00 AM–3:00 PM Pacific Standard Time (PST).



Consistent availability during these hours is required. The position involves regular communication with U.S.-based management, advisors, vendors, and other business contacts.



Confidentiality

Because this position will have access to highly sensitive information—including financial records, bank and payment information, payroll information, employee information, client information, and other confidential business data—a Confidentiality Agreement/NDA will be required as a condition of employment.



The successful candidate must demonstrate a high level of discretion, integrity, and professionalism at all times.



What We Offer

Competitive compensation based on experience and qualifications

Full-time, long-term employment

Fully remote work

Consistent Monday–Friday schedule

Opportunity for professional growth

Direct interaction with company ownership

Collaboration with an experienced financial advisor and tax team

A meaningful role with significant responsibility and ownership



How to Apply

Please submit your updated resume/CV along with a brief response addressing the following:



How many years of experience do you have working directly with U.S.-based companies?

How many separate companies, LLCs, or sets of books have you managed simultaneously?

Describe your hands-on experience with QuickBooks Online.

Describe your experience managing U.S. payroll, accounts payable, accounts receivable, and monthly financial reporting.

What types of U.S. businesses or LLC structures have you worked with?

Describe your level of proficiency with Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets.



Please confirm that you are available to work Monday–Friday, 6:00 AM–3:00 PM PST.



Important

Please apply only if you meet the core requirements of this position.



A Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field, 3–5+ years of progressive accounting experience, U.S. accounting experience, multi-entity accounting experience, and strong QuickBooks Online proficiency are required.



Applicants who demonstrate significant hands-on experience independently managing multiple sets of books for U.S.-based companies will receive strong consideration.

title: Video Editor — Art Channel (Premiere Pro, ongoing)
description:
Stable, recurring part-time video editing work for an art YouTube channel + social media. We make multicam painting process tutorials: satisfying, color-rich, music-synced. Hiring one editor, long-term.

Scope of work

Work is paid per project. One project is the full set of deliverables cut from a single filmed painting tutorial:

• 1 long-form YouTube edit  ~10–15 min, from pre-synced multicam footage

• 2
 
 — 3–5 min, reframed to square

• 4 vertical Shorts/Reels

Rate is agreed per project and discussed with shortlisted applicants. Volume is currently around two projects a month, with room to grow.

Turnaround: long-form first cut within 5 business days; Shorts and cutdowns within 3 days.

Revisions: 3 consolidated rounds per deliverable included.

Required

• 3+ years editing professionally

• Expert-level Premiere Pro (not Final Cut, not DaVinci, not CapCut)

• Strong color grading

• Strong spoken and written English — we use
 for day-to-day messaging and have live calls when needed

• Google Drive

The style

Process videos (painting tutorial), no talking head. The artist is the subject, and the painting process is the focus.

• Satisfying and dynamic — the painting has rhythm. Pacing that breathes: fast when the pour demands it, slow when the detail does.

• Color-led — consistent grading across 3–4 camera angles.

• Music-synced — reveals and cuts land on the beat.

• Short-form with the same feel — satisfying and dynamic, focused on the art process, the beautiful details and reveal.

This is a specialist style. If your experience is mostly talking-head, gaming, or corporate video, this role likely isn’t the right fit. Reference videos — both long-form and short-form —  will be shared with shortlisted applicants.

Portfolio required — applications without a portfolio will not be reviewed

Process

Submit your application ? complete paid edit test with real footage ? begin a trial period if selected. We’re hiring one editor for the long term, not a one-off project.

To apply, reply with

1. Your portfolio — 2–4 full long-form edits that best match the work described above, plus up to 5 short-form edits (YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, or similar). Send published links we can watch in a browser, not files to download. If you were not the only editor working on a project, specify exactly which parts of the video were completed by you.

2. In 2–3 sentences: what makes a video tutorial satisfying to watch?

3. Availability: your time zone, the hours per week you can commit, and whether the turnaround above is realistic for you.

Begin your reply with the word PHTHALO so we know you read this in full.

Serious applicants only. Applications that skip the questions or the code word are not reviewed.

title: Executive Assistant
description:
The Mission of This Role 🎯



Protect the Founder’s time, attention, and energy so he can remain focused on the highest-value activities of the organization.



The Executive Assistant will take ownership of four primary areas:



. Phone. Calendar. Problems.



Success means fewer interruptions, fewer unnecessary decisions, a cleaner calendar, faster communication, and significantly less administrative work reaching the Founder.



Primary Responsibilities

📧 1. Executive
 & Inbox Management



Take primary responsibility for managing the Founder’s business
 inbox.



Responsibilities include:📋



✅Review and organize incoming
 throughout the business day.

✅Identify messages requiring immediate executive attention.

✅Separate important communication from routine requests and low-priority correspondence.

✅Respond to routine
s on the Founder’s behalf when appropriate.

✅Draft responses for executive review when personal involvement is required.

✅Delegate requests to the appropriate team member.

✅Follow up with employees, vendors, carrier representatives, clients, and business partners.

✅Archive, organize, flag, and categorize messages.

✅Maintain outstanding follow-up items so important communication does not fall through the cracks.

✅Reduce the number of
s the Founder personally needs to review or respond to.



Goal: The Founder should spend as little time as reasonably possible managing his own inbox.



📞 2. Phone Call & Voi
 Management



Serve as the first line of defense for incoming calls and voi
s.



Responsibilities include:📋



✅Screen incoming business calls when appropriate.

✅Review missed calls and voi
s.

✅Determine the urgency and appropriate next action.

✅Return routine calls or coordinate responses when authorized.

✅Route callers to the appropriate member of the Legacy Insurance Group team.

✅Schedule calls requiring the Founder’s involvement.

✅Provide concise summaries before important callbacks.

✅Protect the Founder from unnecessary interruptions and unsolicited calls.



The Executive Assistant should become skilled at determining:



Does Sean actually need to handle this—or can I solve it, delegate it, or route it somewhere else?



📅 3. Executive Calendar Management



Own and protect the Founder’s calendar.



Responsibilities include:📋



✅Schedule and coordinate internal and external meetings.

✅Confirm appointments and meeting logistics.

✅Prevent unnecessary meetings from consuming executive time.

✅Resolve scheduling conflicts.

✅Create appropriate buffers between meetings.

✅Reschedule appointments when priorities change.

✅Ensure the Founder has the necessary information before important meetings.

✅Coordinate meetings with employees, vendors, carrier representatives, clients, recruits, and strategic partners.

✅Maintain dedicated time for strategic work and other high-priority responsibilities.

✅Anticipate scheduling issues before they become problems.



The calendar should reflect the Founder’s priorities—not simply other people's requests for his time.



🔥 4. Handle Small Problems Before They Become Big Problems



A major responsibility of this position is preventing minor operational issues from unnecessarily reaching the Founder.



When a problem arises, the Executive Assistant should first ask:



Can I solve this?



If not:



Who on the team can solve this?



Only issues that genuinely require executive authority, judgment, or involvement should be escalated.



Examples may include:📋



✅Coordinating with vendors.

✅Following up on outstanding requests.

✅Tracking down missing information.

✅Resolving scheduling conflicts.

✅Coordinating communication between team members.

✅Researching solutions to minor operational problems.

✅Following up with carrier representatives.

✅Handling routine administrative requests.

✅Identifying the appropriate person to own an issue.

✅Making reasonable decisions within established authority.

✅Ensuring delegated tasks actually get completed.



We want someone who does not simply report problems.



We want someone who solves problems.



Additional Responsibilities



The Executive Assistant may also assist with:📋



✅Preparing meeting agendas and executive summaries.

✅Tracking important commitments and deadlines.

✅Coordinating travel arrangements and itineraries.

✅Preparing documents and presentations.

✅Maintaining confidential executive information.

✅Conducting basic research.

✅Following up on delegated projects.

✅Coordinating recruiting interviews and candidate scheduling.

✅Organizing leadership meetings.

✅Maintaining executive task lists.

✅Documenting recurring processes.

✅Identifying opportunities to automate or delegate repetitive administrative work.

✅Supporting special projects assigned by the Founder.



What Success Looks Like



Within the first several months, the right person should create a noticeable reduction in the amount of administrative work reaching the Founder.



Success will look like:🏆



✅The executive inbox is consistently organized and under control.

✅Important
s receive timely responses.

✅Routine
s are handled without executive involvement.

✅Missed calls and voi
s are screened and appropriately routed.

✅The Founder receives concise summaries rather than having to investigate issues himself.

✅The calendar is organized around strategic priorities.

✅Low-value meetings and interruptions are reduced.

✅Minor problems are solved independently.

✅Delegated tasks are followed through to completion.

✅Important commitments do not fall through the cracks.

✅The Founder spends substantially more time on strategy, leadership, recruiting, systems, sales, marketing, relationships, and organizational growth.



Who We Are Looking For🔍



The ideal candidate is someone who is:



🥇Highly Organized



You naturally create order from chaos and can manage many moving pieces without losing track of details.



🥇Proactive



You don't wait to be told every next step. You anticipate what needs to happen and take action.



🥇Resourceful



When you encounter something you don't know, your instinct is to figure it out.



🥇Decisive



You are comfortable making reasonable decisions without constantly seeking approval.



🥇An Excellent Communicator



You communicate clearly, professionally, and concisely with executives, employees, clients, vendors, and business partners.



🥇Discreet



You understand that working directly with a Founder means having access to confidential business and personal information.



🥇Persistent



If someone owes you an answer, document, confirmation, or deliverable, you follow through until it gets done.



🥇Comfortable With Technology



You can quickly learn communication platforms, calendars, CRM systems, automation tools, AI tools, and other business software.



🥇Calm Under Pressure



When several things happen at once, you prioritize instead of panic.



🥇Ownership-Oriented



You don't say:



"Nobody got back to me."



You say:



"It wasn't resolved, so I followed up, found the right person, and got it handled."



The Most Important Question in This Role🎯



Before bringing something to the Founder, ask:



“Does this truly require the Founder’s time, authority, or judgment?”



If the answer is no, take ownership of getting it resolved.



If the answer is yes, bring the issue forward with the relevant information and a recommended solution.



Instead of:



“Sean, we have a problem. What do you want me to do?”



We prefer:



“Sean, here's the situation. I looked into it and see two options. I recommend Option A because of X. Unless you disagree, I'll move forward with that.”



Qualifications🥅



Preferred qualifications include:



✅3+ years of Executive Assistant, Administrative Assistant, Office Management, Operations, or similar experience.

✅Experience directly supporting a Founder, CEO, President, or senior executive strongly preferred.

✅Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.

✅Strong
 and calendar management skills.

✅Excellent attention to detail.

✅Strong judgment and problem-solving ability.

✅Ability to prioritize competing demands.

✅Comfortable communicating with senior-level business professionals.

✅Experience working with Microsoft Outlook and Microsoft 365 preferred.

✅Familiarity with CRM and business communication systems is helpful.

✅Strong proficiency with modern AI and productivity tools is a plus.

✅Insurance experience is helpful but not required.



Our Culture



Legacy Insurance Group operates with a high-performance mentality.



We believe in:



🎯Taking 100% Ownership — Own the outcome, not the excuse.



🎯Making Decisions — Gather the information, make the best decision available, and move forward.



🎯Continuous Improvement — Get 1% better every day.



🎯Thinking Big — Look beyond today's problem and consider how the organization can operate better tomorrow.



🎯Being Resourceful — Find answers and solutions instead of waiting for instructions.



🎯Teamwork — The organization wins when everyone executes their role at a high level.



🎯Never Giving Up — Persistence and resilience are part of who we are.



Why This Role Matters



As Legacy Insurance Group grows, the Founder & Chief Risk Officer must increasingly focus on responsibilities that cannot easily be delegated:



✅Strategic vision and business planning

✅Recruiting and developing exceptional talent

✅Building scalable systems and processes

✅Sales and marketing strategy

✅Developing strategic relationships

✅Leadership and culture

✅Identifying new opportunities for growth



Every hour spent sorting
s, listening to routine voi
s, coordinating calendars, chasing information, or solving minor administrative problems is an hour that cannot be invested in those responsibilities.



Your job is to give those hours back.



The right Executive Assistant will become one of the most trusted and valuable people in the organization—not simply by helping the Founder accomplish more, but by progressively reducing the number of things that require his involvement.



The Ultimate Goal🥅



Make the Founder less necessary to the day-to-day operation of the business.



Protect his time.



Protect his attention.



Solve what you can.



Delegate what others can solve.



Escalate only what truly requires him.



And help build an organization that can operate effectively without everything flowing through one person.

🌙 EVENING / LATE-SHIFT VIRTUAL ASSISTANT — SHORT-TERM RENTAL / AIRBNB OPERATIONS



Hours: 2pm – 10pm UK time, Monday to Friday — with weekend cover on a rotation

Start: ASAP



NEED HOSTAWAY EXPERIENCE 



Applications without the video and CV won't be reviewed.



👉 





We're a UK short-term rental management company running a portfolio of apartments and houses across Bristol, Cardiff and London. We're growing fast, and we need an experienced operator to hold the desk through the afternoon and evening. Guests don't stop messaging at 9pm, and lockboxes don't stop failing after office hours.



This is not an entry-level role. You'll be running the desk largely on your own, making judgement calls without someone sitting next to you to check with. If you haven't done this before, this isn't the one for you.



WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING



Guest communication — the bulk of the job



Answering guest messages across Airbnb, 
, WhatsApp, direct enquiries and the PMS inbox — fast, warm, and in our brand voice

Handling enquiries and converting them into bookings: availability, pricing questions, minimum stays, long-stay requests

Running the check-in flow — arrival details, door codes, directions, parking info — and troubleshooting the guest standing outside at 9pm who can't get in

Handling in-stay complaints and issues: no hot water, noisy neighbours, a broken appliance, a missing amenity. De-escalating, resolving what you can, escalating what you can't

Check-out reminders, late check-out requests, extension requests

Reviews — responding to them, and spotting the problem that's about to become a bad one before it lands



Bookings and calendar



Processing new bookings, alterations, extensions and cancellations

Keeping calendars accurate across every channel; catching and fixing sync issues before they double-book us

Monitoring payment status, chasing outstanding balances, flagging failed payments

Security deposits — checking they've been collected and flagging what hasn't



Operations and coordination



Logging every open issue on our task board with enough detail that the next person can act on it without re-investigating

Coordinating with cleaners, handymen and contractors — raising jobs, chasing ETAs, confirming completion

Ordering replacements and consumables when something breaks or runs out, and tracking delivery through to the guest

Monitoring property health — catching the small thing tonight that becomes the 1-star review on Friday



Handover and reporting



Clocking in with a full sweep of every channel, then posting a shift report

Posting a clean end-of-shift handover: open guest issues, money, maintenance, landlord items, and anything needing a decision from the founders

Owning your items through to closed. No "I'll leave it for the day team"



Admin



Landlord and owner queries, basic invoicing support, expense logging

Keeping listing information and property data accurate

Contributing to our SOPs — when you solve something new, you write it down so nobody has to solve it twice



WHAT YOU NEED



✅ Minimum 3 years' experience in short-term rental / Airbnb management or property operations. Please don't apply without it — applications under 3 years will not be reviewed

✅ Hands-on with a PMS — Hostaway, Guesty, Hospitable, Lodgify or similar

✅ Confident inside the Airbnb, 
 and VRBO extranets

✅ Excellent written English — you are the voice of the company to every guest

✅ Genuinely comfortable working these hours, largely alone, with minimal supervision

✅ Happy to take your turn on the weekend rotation

✅ Sound judgement under pressure. You'll hit situations no SOP covers. We want someone who thinks, d
 and documents, not someone who waits eight hours for a reply

✅ Reliable power, internet and a proper working setup

✅ Organised to the point of being annoying about it



Nice to have: Slack, 
, PriceLabs, Stripe, KrispCall or a similar VOIP, and experience with UK properties



WHAT WE OFFER

title: Right Hand to Business Owner: Operations Lead, EA & Evening Point Person
description:
POSITION OVERVIEW

We are a growing property management firm managing luxury STRs in Tennessee and an LTR portfolio in Minnesota. We are not looking for a task-doer. We are looking for the owner's right hand: a proactive, system-minded leader who can run our evenings and weekends like they own them, help lead new projects and initiatives with the owner, and develop and improve the internal systems we run on.



WHY THIS ROLE:

 We're looking for a team member who will take ownership, think creatively, and contribute to refining our systems as we grow. We're excited to build a lasting relationship with someone in this role, ensuring you feel supported, trusted, and empowered to make decisions. This isn't a role for a task-doer or someone who is most comfortable in a role that primarily involves following a checklist. This is a role for a creative problem-solver with a high EQ and excellent communication skills and follow-through.



Real Authority: You'll have real authority to resolve issues, including a spending limit. When something breaks at 9PM, you are the decision-maker, not a message-forwarder. The owner should hear about most problems after they've been solved. This is a high-trust position, and that trust will be earned: your authority grows as you demonstrate judgment.



A Seat That Grows: This role is built to grow into an overall management position across the business, on evidence, not promises. You'll work directly with the owner and act as the connective layer for our small team.



Growth-Minded & Solutions-Focused: We don't dwell on problems; we find solutions. We want people who are hungry to learn, grow, and improve our systems every day.



Positive Energy: Property management and guest hospitality involve surprise challenges. Pipes burst, guests lock themselves out. We approach our work with a positive attitude and a "can-do" spirit.



A Relationship, Not a Transaction: We want a years-long partnership. Impact over activity: you won't be micromanaged; you'll be given clear goals, real trust, and the freedom to execute.



This role is approximately 40 hours per week. Your compensation will reflect your experience, initiative, growth, and contribution to the business's success.



Please explain your schedule availability. how flexible are you? what is your preferred schedule? US daytime hours, Swing shift, Night shift or any? What days or nights are you unavailable?





YOUR CORE MISSION



Evenings & Weekend Command (about half your time):

During your shift, you are the front line and the d
 for the whole business. Guest messages and check-in issues at our Tennessee cabins. Urgent tenant and contractor issues in Minnesota. The surprise problems that don't respect business hours. Your job is to resolve them with judgment and calm, using your authority and our established playbooks, so the owner's evening stays quiet. Success is measured by how rarely problems need to reach him, and how completely they're handled when he reads about them the next morning.



Operations & Loop-Closing (about a third):

The "Loop-Closer": when a task comes in, you manage the communication, the schedule, and the reporting in 
 and in daily report-outs to the team. You make sure work moves from "reported" to "fully completed," and that everyone involved has what they need. You coordinate repairs and vendors, maintain inventory across properties, oversee move-in/move-out procedures, document interactions, and identify potential issues before they become problems. You work alongside our STR specialist and our LTR property manager as the connective layer between them and the owner.



Special Projects & Marketing (the remainder):

You take on the owner's next-most-important thing: marketing pushes 
 campaigns, social, listing platforms), process building, research, and whatever the business needs next. This is where the role grows.



ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS:

3+ years working in a US-based business with operations responsibility.



High C2 fluency in English: Confident in multi-person meetings, initiating phone calls, and in non-scripted situations in English.

Proven judgment: You have made real decisions with real stakes, without waiting for permission, and you can tell us about them specifically.

The "Loop-Closer" DNA: You live by the 24-hour no-update rule. If a project is open, you provide an update before we have to ask.

Highly detail-oriented and organized: Able to track tasks across multiple properties, prioritize by urgency and importance, and follow up on outstanding issues.

A positive growth mindset, and proactive communication: you don't wait to be asked for updates, and you're receptive to feedback.

Availability for the exact schedule above, reliably, long-term.



The Tech Stack: We use Google Workspace, OwnerRez, 
, and a variety of specialized tools. We value your operations judgment over your specific software experience; if you've run comparable tools, we can train you on our stack.



MUST HAVE reliable internet connection with backup.

Proficiency with Google Drive, WhatsApp, and ability to quickly learn 
.



HOW TO APPLY:



To verify your attention to detail, please follow these steps exactly:



Subject Line: Include the name of the original bass player for the Grateful Dead.



Cover Letter (Paragraph 3): Include the phrase "closing the loop."



In your response, confirm you are available for the exact days and times described above.



1) Describe a specific time you solved an urgent problem without waiting for direction. How did it start, what steps did you take, what did it cost, and how was it resolved?



2) Describe a time you spent your employer's money (or made a binding decision) on your own authority to fix a problem. What was the situation, what did you d
, and how did your boss react?



3)  At any moment you'll have multiple open items running: say a repair waiting on a contractor, an unhappy guest, and a supply order all live at once. Two things: (1) What system do you personally use to track these so nothing slips and everyone gets an update before they have to ask? (2) When you can't get to everything, how do you d
 what comes first? Give a real example showing both.



Please include a resume or summary of your background. If you have professional recommendations from previous US-based employers, we strongly encourage you to include them.



4), tell us how your previous experience sets you up to excel in this role. We're especially interested in where you've led or developed people, built or improved systems, and operated with real autonomy.



A note on AI: We use it too, so use whatever tools help you. That said, we receive many applications with viirtually identical answers to our application questions, which are obviously written by AI. 

We'd much prefer to read about your real experience, in detail, in your own words. However you use AI,  we ask one thing in return: be straight about what you've actually done and how you actually communicate. And tell us two things: how you used AI to put this application together, and how you'd use it in the day-to-day of this role.
